records.source: ה֥וֹי הַחֹֽקְקִ֖ים חִקְקֵי־אָ֑וֶן וּֽמְכַתְּבִ֥ים עָמָ֖ל כִּתֵּֽבוּ׃
records.gloss: Woe, those decreeing decrees of wickedness, and writers [of] trouble [who] write,
pieces: Woe to those who make wicked statutes, \q and to the scribes who keep writing out misery,

L.1: Woe, those who decree decrees of wickedness, \q and writers [who] write trouble,

R.1: How terrible it will be for those who make evil laws, \q for the officials who write rules that bring people trouble!

decisions.choice: woe: the last of a series of woes
decisions.reason: The cry of grief and warning takes up the woes of 5:8-23. This one is aimed at those who use the law itself to rob the weak.

decisions.choice: write trouble: put oppression into writing
decisions.reason: The word means toil, trouble or misery. The scribes write documents and rulings that bring hardship on others, so the harm is done with the authority of written law. The verb form suggests they keep on doing it.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into verse 2
decisions.reason: Verse 2 says what these laws are for, so the record ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: officials who write rules
decisions.reason: The writers are those who draft legal rulings for the court; Readable names them as officials.

records.heading: Woe to those who write wicked statutes

records.source: לְהַטּ֤וֹת מִדִּין֙ דַּלִּ֔ים וְלִגְזֹ֕ל מִשְׁפַּ֖ט עֲנִיֵּ֣י עַמִּ֑י לִהְי֤וֹת אַלְמָנוֹת֙ שְׁלָלָ֔ם וְאֶת־יְתוֹמִ֖ים יָבֹֽזּוּ׃
records.gloss: to turn aside from judgment [the] poor and to take away [the] justice of [the] poor of my people, to be widows their prey, and the fatherless they plunder.
pieces: to push the needy away from a fair hearing \q and strip the poor among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people of their rights, \q so that widows become their spoil \q and orphans their loot.

L.2: to turn aside the poor from judgment \q and to rob the afflicted of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people [of their] justice, \q that widows may be their prey \q and [that] they may plunder the fatherless.

R.2: They keep poor people from getting a fair trial. \q They take away the rights of the needy among {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people. \q They rob widows and steal from children who have no father.

decisions.choice: judgment, justice: a fair hearing and the rights it protects
decisions.reason: The first word is the legal case or verdict; the second is justice, a person's right before the law. The needy are turned away from the court, and their rights are taken from them.

decisions.choice: my people: the LORD speaking
decisions.reason: As in 3:12-15, the LORD calls the poor "my people". Those who rob them rob his own.

decisions.choice: widows and the fatherless: those with no man to defend them in court
decisions.reason: In Israel a widow or an orphan had no husband or father to speak for them at the gate, where cases were heard. The law put them under God's own care (Exodus 22:21-23; Deuteronomy 10:18), and Isaiah's first chapter called for justice for them (1:17, 23).

decisions.choice: They keep ... They take ... They rob
decisions.reason: Readable ends the sentence of verse 1 and states the purpose of the laws as what the lawmakers do.

records.source: וּמַֽה־תַּעֲשׂוּ֙ לְי֣וֹם פְּקֻדָּ֔ה וּלְשׁוֹאָ֖ה מִמֶּרְחָ֣ק תָּב֑וֹא עַל־מִי֙ תָּנ֣וּסוּ לְעֶזְרָ֔ה וְאָ֥נָה תַעַזְב֖וּ כְּבוֹדְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And what will you do for [the] day of punishment, and for the devastation [that] from far will come? To whom will you flee for help, and where will you leave your wealth?
pieces: What will you do on the day you are called to account, \q when ruin comes sweeping in from far away? \q Whom will you flee to for help? \q And where will you leave your wealth behind?

L.3: And what will you do on [the] day of visitation, \q and in the devastation [that] will come from afar? \q To whom will you flee for help, \q and where will you leave your wealth?

R.3: What will you do when the day comes for you to be punished? \q What will you do when disaster comes on you from a faraway land? \q Who will you run to for help? \q Where will you hide your riches?

decisions.choice: day of visitation: the day God calls to account
decisions.reason: The word is from the verb "visit, attend to". When God visits wrongdoers, he calls them to account and punishes (the verb in verse 12). The day is a time of judgment.

decisions.choice: devastation: a storm of ruin
decisions.reason: The word means a sudden ruin, like a storm that lays waste. "From afar" points to an army from a distant land, the Assyrians of verse 5 (5:26).

decisions.choice: wealth: riches, often thought of as one's weight and honor
decisions.reason: The word for wealth comes from the root "be heavy", the root of "glory". The riches taken from the poor cannot be carried away or kept safe on that day.

decisions.choice: hide
decisions.reason: "Leave" means to leave in safekeeping; Readable says "hide" to make the point clear: there will be no safe place for it.

records.source: בִּלְתִּ֤י כָרַע֙ תַּ֣חַת אַסִּ֔יר וְתַ֥חַת הֲרוּגִ֖ים יִפֹּ֑לוּ בְּכָל־זֹאת֙ לֹא־שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: Except [one] crouches under prisoner[s], and under [the] slain they will fall. In all this not has turned back his anger, and still his hand [is] stretched out.
pieces: Nothing is left but to crouch down among the captives \q or to fall among the dead. \q Even so, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger has not turned back; \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand is still stretched out.

L.4: [Nothing remains] except [that one] crouches among [the] prisoners, \q and among [the] slain they fall. \q For all this {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger has not turned back, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand [is] still stretched out.

R.4: All you will be able to do is kneel down with the prisoners \q or lie among the dead. \q Even after all this, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is still angry. \q His hand is still raised to strike.

decisions.choice: except one crouches: there is no way out but captivity or death
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is very compressed: "except one crouches under prisoners, and under the slain they fall". It means that the only choices left are to bow down among the captives or to fall among the dead. "Under" may mean among them or beneath them, crushed under the heap.

decisions.choice: his anger has not turned back: the refrain of 5:25 and 9:11, 16, 20
decisions.reason: The same refrain closes each stanza of the poem that begins in 9:7 (Hebrew numbering) and goes back to 5:25. Here it closes the poem: the judgment is not over yet.

decisions.choice: the LORD is still angry
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD as the one whose anger has not turned back, and explains the stretched-out hand as a hand raised to strike.

records.source: ה֥וֹי אַשּׁ֖וּר שֵׁ֣בֶט אַפִּ֑י וּמַטֶּה־ה֥וּא בְיָדָ֖ם זַעְמִֽי׃
records.gloss: Woe, Assyria, [the] rod of my anger, and a staff it [is] in their hand, my indignation.
pieces: Woe to Assyria, the rod of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger! \q The club they hold in their hand is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} indignation.

L.5: Woe, Assyria, [the] rod of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger, \q and the staff in their hand [is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} indignation!

R.5: How terrible it will be for Assyria! I use Assyria like a stick to punish when I am angry. \q The club they swing is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fury.

decisions.choice: Assyria, the rod of my anger: the tool God uses to punish
decisions.reason: The woe now turns on Assyria itself. God calls it the rod he swings in his anger. The great empire is only a stick in his hand (verse 15); it will be punished in its turn for its pride (verse 12). The rod of verses 5, 15 and 24 returns in 14:5 and 30:31.

decisions.choice: a staff it is in their hand, my indignation: the staff they hold is God's fury
alternatives: a staff of my indignation is in their hand
decisions.reason: The second line is compressed. It most likely means that the club in the Assyrians' hand is God's own indignation at work. "Their" is the Assyrian people; in verse 6 the nation is spoken of as "him".

decisions.choice: I use Assyria like a stick to punish
decisions.reason: Readable unpacks the image of the rod into a sentence.

records.heading: Assyria, the rod of my anger

records.source: בְּג֤וֹי חָנֵף֙ אֲשַׁלְּחֶ֔נּוּ וְעַל־עַ֥ם עֶבְרָתִ֖י אֲצַוֶּ֑נּוּ לִשְׁלֹ֤ל שָׁלָל֙ וְלָבֹ֣ז בַּ֔ז וּלְשׂוּמ֥וֹ מִרְמָ֖ס כְּחֹ֥מֶר חוּצֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Against a nation godless I send him, and against [the] people of my wrath I command him, to plunder plunder and to take spoil spoil, and to make it a trampling like [the] mud of [the] streets.
pieces: I send him against a corrupt nation; \q against the people who stir {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath I give him orders, \q to carry off spoil and haul away plunder, \q and to stamp them into the ground like mud in the streets.

L.6: Against a godless nation I send him, \q and against the people of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath I command him, \q to plunder plunder and to seize spoil, \q and to make it a trampled place like the mud of [the] streets.

R.6: I send the Assyrians against a nation that does not respect {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q I order them to attack the people who have made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry. \q I order them to carry off everything those people own and to stomp on them like mud in the street.

decisions.choice: godless: corrupt, without reverence for God
decisions.reason: The word describes someone who is defiled and has turned from God while still keeping up appearances (9:16, Hebrew numbering). The nation is God's own people, Judah and Israel ("the people of my wrath").

decisions.choice: to plunder plunder and to take spoil spoil: the name of Isaiah's son
decisions.reason: The same two words make up the name Maher-shalal-hash-baz, "Swift to the spoil, quick to the plunder" (8:1, 3). What that name foretold is now God's order to Assyria.

decisions.choice: to make it: the reading of the margin
decisions.reason: The written text and the reading in the margin differ only in the spelling of the verb "make"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the Assyrians ... them
decisions.reason: "Him" is Assyria, spoken of as one person. Readable names the Assyrians and uses "them".

records.source: וְהוּא֙ לֹא־כֵ֣ן יְדַמֶּ֔ה וּלְבָב֖וֹ לֹא־כֵ֣ן יַחְשֹׁ֑ב כִּ֚י לְהַשְׁמִ֣יד בִּלְבָב֔וֹ וּלְהַכְרִ֥ית גּוֹיִ֖ם לֹ֥א מְעָֽט׃
records.gloss: And he not so intends, and his heart not so plans; for to destroy [is] in his heart, and to cut off nations not a few.
pieces: But that is not what he has in view; \q that is not the plan in his heart. \q What he has at heart is to wipe out and cut down nations, and not a few.

L.7: But he does not intend so, \q and his heart does not plan so; \q for to destroy [is] in his heart, \q and to cut off nations, not a few.

R.7: But the king of Assyria does not think of it this way. \q That is not what he plans. \q All he wants is to destroy many nations and wipe them out.

decisions.choice: he does not intend so: Assyria does not know it serves God
decisions.reason: God sends Assyria to punish (verse 6), but Assyria has its own aim: conquest for its own glory. The same events are God's purpose and Assyria's ambition, and God holds Assyria to account for its aim (verses 12-15).

decisions.choice: heart: the mind and will
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is where one thinks and plans, not only where one feels.

decisions.choice: the king of Assyria
decisions.reason: Readable names the king, who speaks in verses 8-11 and is named in verse 12.

records.source: כִּ֖י יֹאמַ֑ר הֲלֹ֥א שָׂרַ֛י יַחְדָּ֖ו מְלָכִֽים׃
records.gloss: For he says, [are] not my commanders altogether kings?
pieces: For he says, \q "My commanders, are they not kings, every one of them?

L.8: For he says, \q "Are not my commanders all of them kings?

R.8: The king of Assyria brags, \q "Every one of my army commanders is as great as a king!

decisions.choice: my commanders ... kings: the boast of the great king
decisions.reason: The Assyrian kings called themselves "king of kings". Conquered kings served as his officers, and his governors had the power of kings. The boast is that his servants are as great as the rulers of other lands.

decisions.choice: he says: the king's speech runs to the end of verse 11
decisions.reason: The quotation opens here and closes at the end of verse 11.

decisions.choice: brags ... as great as a king
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies and names the speaker.

records.source: הֲלֹ֥א כְּכַרְכְּמִ֖ישׁ כַּלְנ֑וֹ אִם־לֹ֤א כְאַרְפַּד֙ חֲמָ֔ת אִם־לֹ֥א כְדַמֶּ֖שֶׂק שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: [Is] not like Carchemish Calno? Or not like Arpad Hamath? Or not like Damascus Samaria?
pieces: Did Calno not go the way of Carchemish? \q Did Hamath not go the way of Arpad, \q and Samaria the way of Damascus?

L.9: [Is] not Calno like Carchemish? \q Or [is] not Hamath like Arpad? \q Or [is] not Samaria like Damascus?

R.9: I conquered the city of Calno just as I conquered Carchemish. \q I took Hamath just as I took Arpad. \q And I took Samaria just as I took Damascus.

decisions.choice: Carchemish, Calno, Arpad, Hamath, Damascus, Samaria: cities Assyria had taken
decisions.reason: Each pair names cities in Syria and Israel that fell one after another to Assyria, moving south toward Jerusalem. Damascus fell to Tiglath-pileser III in 732 BC, and Samaria fell in 722 BC. Calno is the Calneh of Amos 6:2. Each city is said to be no different from the one before it.

decisions.choice: is not ... like: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: The questions mean: each city fell just like the last. None of them could stand, and the king expects Jerusalem to be next.

decisions.choice: I conquered ... I took
decisions.reason: Readable states the point of the questions as the king's boast.

records.source: כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ מָצְאָ֣ה יָדִ֔י לְמַמְלְכֹ֖ת הָאֱלִ֑יל וּפְסִ֣ילֵיהֶ֔ם מִירֽוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וּמִשֹּׁמְרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Just as has found my hand the kingdoms of the idol, and their images [were] more than Jerusalem and than Samaria,
pieces: Just as my hand laid hold of kingdoms full of idols, \q whose carved images outnumbered those of Jerusalem and Samaria,

L.10: Just as my hand has reached the kingdoms of the idol, \q and their images [were more] than Jerusalem's and Samaria's,

R.10: I have captured kingdoms that had more idols than Jerusalem and Samaria.

decisions.choice: idol, images: worthless gods and carved figures
decisions.reason: The first word means "worthless thing, nothing", Isaiah's word for false gods (2:8, 18, 20). The second is a carved figure. Isaiah lets the king of Assyria speak of the gods of nations as worthless idols, as he goes on to treat the LORD as one more of them.

decisions.choice: more than Jerusalem and Samaria: greater in number or in power
decisions.reason: The boast is that the gods of the conquered kingdoms were greater than those of Jerusalem and Samaria, yet they did not save their peoples (36:18-20; 37:12-13).

decisions.choice: I have captured ...
decisions.reason: Readable makes the comparison of verses 10-11 two separate sentences.

records.source: הֲלֹ֗א כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֛יתִי לְשֹׁמְר֖וֹן וְלֶאֱלִילֶ֑יהָ כֵּ֛ן אֶעֱשֶׂ֥ה לִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וְלַעֲצַבֶּֽיהָ׃ס
records.gloss: Not just as I did to Samaria and to its idols so I will do to Jerusalem and to its images?
pieces: what I did to Samaria and its idols, \q will I not do the same to Jerusalem and its images?"

L.11: Shall I not, just as I did to Samaria and to her idols, \q so do to Jerusalem and to her images?"

R.11: I destroyed Samaria and its idols. \q Now I will do the same thing to Jerusalem and its idols!"

decisions.choice: Samaria ... Jerusalem: the king counts the LORD among the idols
decisions.reason: To the king of Assyria, Jerusalem's God is one more idol like those of Samaria. This is the pride for which God will punish him (verse 12; 36:18-20; 37:23).

decisions.choice: not ... so I will do: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: The question means "of course I will". It ends the king's speech that began in verse 8.

records.source: וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי־יְבַצַּ֤ע אֲדֹנָי֙ אֶת־כָּל־מַֽעֲשֵׂ֔הוּ בְּהַ֥ר צִיּ֖וֹן וּבִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם אֶפְקֹ֗ד עַל־פְּרִי־גֹ֨דֶל֙ לְבַ֣ב מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֔וּר וְעַל־תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת ר֥וּם עֵינָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And it will be when finishes [the] Lord all his work on [the] mountain of Zion and in Jerusalem, I will visit on [the] fruit of [the] greatness of [the] heart of [the] king of Assyria and on [the] glory of [the] haughtiness of his eyes.
pieces: When the Lord has completed everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is doing on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, \q I will punish what has grown from the swollen pride of the king of Assyria, \q and the glory of his haughty look.

L.12: And it will be, when the Lord finishes all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, \q I will punish the fruit of the greatness of heart of the king of Assyria, \q and the glory of the haughtiness of his eyes.

R.12: The Lord will finish all {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has planned to do on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem. \q Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says: I will punish the king of Assyria for his proud heart and for the arrogant look in his eyes.

decisions.choice: I will punish: the speaker moves from "the Lord" to "I"
decisions.reason: The verse begins by speaking of the Lord and then has him say "I". This shift of person is common in the prophets: the prophet speaks of God, and then God speaks for himself.

decisions.choice: when the Lord finishes all his work: the judgment on Zion has a limit
decisions.reason: God's work of discipline on Jerusalem by means of Assyria will run its course and then stop. After that, the tool will be judged (verses 24-27).

decisions.choice: the fruit of the greatness of heart ... the glory of the haughtiness of his eyes: arrogance and its results
decisions.reason: A "great heart" is pride (9:8, Hebrew numbering), and lifted-up eyes are an arrogant look (2:11; 5:15). The "fruit" is what the pride has produced: the boasting of verses 8-11 and the deeds behind it.

decisions.choice: Then he says:
decisions.reason: Readable marks the change from speaking about the Lord to the Lord speaking.

records.source: כִּ֣י אָמַ֗ר בְּכֹ֤חַ יָדִי֙ עָשִׂ֔יתִי וּבְחָכְמָתִ֖י כִּ֣י נְבֻנ֑וֹתִי וְאָסִ֣יר׀גְּבוּלֹ֣ת עַמִּ֗ים וַעֲתוּדֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ שׁוֹשֵׂ֔תִי וְאוֹרִ֥יד כַּאבִּ֖יר יוֹשְׁבִֽים׃
records.gloss: For he says, by [the] strength of my hand I have done [it], and by my wisdom, for I have understanding; and I have removed [the] borders of peoples, and their treasures I have plundered, and I have brought down like a mighty one those sitting.
pieces: For he says, "My own strong hand has done this, \q and my wisdom, for I am shrewd. \q I wiped away the borders between peoples and stripped their storehouses bare; \q like a mighty bull I toppled those who sat on thrones.

L.13: For he says, "By the strength of my hand I have done [it], \q and by my wisdom, for I have understanding; \q and I removed the borders of peoples, and their treasures I plundered, \q and like a mighty one I brought down those sitting [enthroned].

R.13: The king of Assyria says, "I did all this by my own power. \q I did it because I am wise and clever. \q I erased the borders between nations. I took their treasures. \q Like a powerful bull, I knocked kings off their thrones.

decisions.choice: their treasures: the reading of the margin
decisions.reason: The reading in the margin means "their stored treasures". The written text has a similar word meaning "what is prepared for them" or "their future". The sense is close either way: he has looted what nations had laid up.

decisions.choice: like a mighty one: like a bull, a strong man
decisions.reason: The word means mighty, and is also used of a bull or a powerful animal (34:7; Psalm 22:13). The written text can also be read "I brought down, mighty as I am".

decisions.choice: those sitting: those enthroned, or the inhabitants
decisions.reason: The word means "those who sit" or "those who dwell". Beside "brought down" it most likely means kings on their thrones, though it may mean the peoples who lived in the lands.

decisions.choice: a mighty bull
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the strength of the word and its picture of a charging bull.

records.source: וַתִּמְצָ֨א כַקֵּ֤ן׀יָדִי֙ לְחֵ֣יל הָֽעַמִּ֔ים וְכֶאֱסֹף֙ בֵּיצִ֣ים עֲזֻב֔וֹת כָּל־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲנִ֣י אָסָ֑פְתִּי וְלֹ֤א הָיָה֙ נֹדֵ֣ד כָּנָ֔ף וּפֹצֶ֥ה פֶ֖ה וּמְצַפְצֵֽף׃
records.gloss: And has found like a nest my hand the wealth of the peoples, and as gathers [one] eggs abandoned all the earth I have gathered, and not was [one] fluttering a wing, and opening a mouth, and chirping.
pieces: My hand found the riches of the peoples as easily as a bird's nest; \q the way someone collects eggs that have been deserted, \q I collected the whole earth. \q No wing fluttered; no beak opened; no peep was heard."

L.14: And my hand has found like a nest the wealth of the peoples, \q and as [one] gathers abandoned eggs, \q I have gathered all the earth; \q and there was none fluttering a wing or opening a mouth or chirping."

R.14: Taking the riches of the nations was as easy as reaching into a bird's nest. \q I gathered up the whole earth the way someone gathers eggs that the mother bird has left. \q No one even flapped a wing or opened a mouth to make a sound!"

decisions.choice: like a nest ... abandoned eggs: plunder taken with no resistance
decisions.reason: The king pictures the nations as a nest whose mother bird has flown away. Robbing it was easy and no one fought back: not a wing moved, not a beak opened.

decisions.choice: I have gathered: the boast ends
decisions.reason: The word "I" is stated for emphasis. The king's speech that began in verse 13 closes here.

records.source: הֲיִתְפָּאֵר֙ הַגַּרְזֶ֔ן עַ֖ל הַחֹצֵ֣ב בּ֑וֹ אִם־יִתְגַּדֵּ֤ל הַמַּשּׂוֹר֙ עַל־מְנִיפ֔וֹ כְּהָנִ֥יף שֵׁ֨בֶט֙ וְאֶת־מְרִימָ֔יו כְּהָרִ֥ים מַטֶּ֖ה לֹא־עֵֽץ׃
records.gloss: Does it glorify itself, the axe, over the one cutting with it? Or does it make itself great, the saw, over the one wielding it? As [if] wielded a rod those lifting it, as [if] lifted a staff [one who is] not wood!
pieces: Can an ax take pride over the one who chops with it, \q or a saw make itself greater than the one who works it? \q That would be like a stick swinging the hands that lift it, \q or a wooden club lifting someone who is not wood!

L.15: Shall the axe glorify itself over the one who cuts with it? \q Or shall the saw make itself great over the one who wields it? \q As if a rod should wield those who lift it, \q as if a staff should lift [one who is] not wood!

R.15: Can an ax brag that it is greater than the person who uses it to chop? \q Can a saw act more important than the person who uses it to cut? \q That is like a stick swinging the person who picks it up! \q A wooden club cannot lift a person. Assyria is only a tool in God's hand.

decisions.choice: axe, saw, rod, staff: Assyria is only God's tool
decisions.reason: God answers the king's boast with a question. A tool cannot boast against the one who uses it; Assyria has done nothing that God did not use it to do (verses 5-6).

decisions.choice: not wood: a living person
decisions.reason: "Not wood" is the one who holds the staff, the living person who is not a piece of timber. The picture is absurd on purpose: a stick lifting the one who holds it.

decisions.choice: Assyria is only a tool in God's hand.
decisions.reason: Readable states the point of the comparison, which verses 5 and 15 together make.

records.source: לָ֠כֵן יְשַׁלַּ֨ח הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת בְּמִשְׁמַנָּ֖יו רָז֑וֹן וְתַ֧חַת כְּבֹד֛וֹ יֵקַ֥ד יְקֹ֖ד כִּיק֥וֹד אֵֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: Therefore will send the Lord, Yahweh of hosts, on his fat ones leanness, and under his glory will be kindled a kindling like [the] kindling of fire.
pieces: So the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies will send a wasting disease into his well-fed troops, \q and beneath his splendor a blaze will flare up like a burning fire.

L.16: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of hosts will send leanness among his fat ones, \q and under his glory a burning will burn like the burning of fire.

R.16: So the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies will send a disease that makes the king of Assyria's strong soldiers waste away. \q Under all his glory, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will light a fire that burns everything.

decisions.choice: leanness among his fat ones: a wasting sickness among strong men
decisions.reason: "Fat ones" are the well-fed, sturdy warriors of the king of Assyria; "leanness" is a disease that wastes the body away (Psalm 106:15). The words look ahead to the sudden end of Assyria's army before Jerusalem in 701 BC (37:36).

decisions.choice: under his glory: the king's pomp, or his army
decisions.reason: "His glory" is the king's splendor and may stand for his army, his nobles and his wealth. The fire burns beneath it, as in a forest, as the next verses go on to picture.

decisions.choice: the Lord, Yahweh of hosts: the title with the article
decisions.reason: The word for Lord here has the article ("the Lord", the master), as in verse 33 and 1:24. The full title stresses that the Master of the armies of heaven acts against the great king.

decisions.choice: the king of Assyria's strong soldiers ... the LORD will light
decisions.reason: Readable names whose men are meant and who lights the fire.

records.source: וְהָיָ֤ה אֽוֹר־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְאֵ֔שׁ וּקְדוֹשׁ֖וֹ לְלֶהָבָ֑ה וּבָעֲרָ֗ה וְאָֽכְלָ֛ה שִׁית֥וֹ וּשְׁמִיר֖וֹ בְּי֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: And will become [the] light of Israel a fire, and its Holy One a flame, and it will burn and it will devour his thorns and his briers in day one.
pieces: The one who is Israel's Light will turn to fire, \q its Holy One to flame; \q it will flare up and burn up his thornbushes and briers, all in a single day.

L.17: And the Light of Israel will become a fire, \q and his Holy One a flame, \q and it will burn and devour his thorns and his briers in one day.

R.17: God, who is the light of Israel, will become like a fire. \q Israel's Holy One will become like a flame. \q In a single day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will burn up the Assyrian army like a fire burns up thorns and weeds.

decisions.choice: the Light of Israel, its Holy One: God himself
decisions.reason: God, who is Israel's light (2:5; 9:1, Hebrew numbering; Psalm 27:1), becomes a fire to its enemies. "Its Holy One" is the Holy One of Israel, Isaiah's name for God (1:4; verse 20).

decisions.choice: his thorns and his briers: the king of Assyria's army
decisions.reason: "His" is the king of Assyria. The pair of words is Isaiah's "thorns and briers" (5:6; 7:23-25; 9:17, Hebrew numbering), here a picture of the Assyrian host, burned like brushwood.

decisions.choice: the Assyrian army like a fire burns up thorns and weeds
decisions.reason: Readable says who the thorns stand for.

records.source: וּכְב֤וֹד יַעְרוֹ֙ וְכַרְמִלּ֔וֹ מִנֶּ֥פֶשׁ וְעַד־בָּשָׂ֖ר יְכַלֶּ֑ה וְהָיָ֖ה כִּמְסֹ֥ס נֹסֵֽס׃
records.gloss: And [the] glory of his forest and his orchard, from soul and to flesh, it will bring to an end, and it will be as wastes away [one who is] sick.
pieces: The splendor of his forest and his orchard land it will wipe out, body and soul, \q and it will be as the strength drains out of a sick man.

L.18: And the glory of his forest and his orchard it will bring to an end, from soul even to flesh, \q and it will be as [when] a sick [man] wastes away.

R.18: The fire will destroy the king's great forests and fine orchards. It will destroy everything, inside and out. \q Assyria will become weak, like a sick person whose strength is gone.

decisions.choice: his forest and his orchard: the might and pride of Assyria
decisions.reason: The king boasts of cutting down the forests of Lebanon (37:24). Now his own "forest", his great army and the glory of his kingdom, is burned (verses 33-34).

decisions.choice: from soul to flesh: completely, inside and out
decisions.reason: "Soul" is the life within, "flesh" the body. The phrase means the whole of it, nothing left.

decisions.choice: as a sick man wastes away
decisions.reason: The two words are rare. They may also mean "as a standard-bearer faints", taking the second word from "banner". The picture of wasting sickness fits verse 16.

records.source: וּשְׁאָ֥ר עֵ֛ץ יַעְר֖וֹ מִסְפָּ֣ר יִֽהְי֑וּ וְנַ֖עַר יִכְתְּבֵֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And [the] remnant of [the] trees of his forest a number will be, and a child will write them.
pieces: What is left of the trees in his forest will be so few \q that a child could list them.

L.19: And the remnant of the trees of his forest will be [few in] number, \q and a child will write them down.

R.19: So few trees will be left in his forest \q that even a child could count them.

decisions.choice: a number: few, able to be counted
decisions.reason: To be "a number" means to be few enough to count (Deuteronomy 33:6). A child who could only just write could list them all.

decisions.choice: remnant: the same word as in verses 20-22
decisions.reason: Assyria will have a small remnant of trees; Israel will have a remnant that returns to God. The word links the two halves of the chapter.

records.source: וְהָיָ֣ה׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא לֹֽא־יוֹסִ֨יף ע֜וֹד שְׁאָ֤ר יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וּפְלֵיטַ֣ת בֵּֽית־יַעֲקֹ֔ב לְהִשָּׁעֵ֖ן עַל־מַכֵּ֑הוּ וְנִשְׁעַ֗ן עַל־יְהוָ֛ה קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֶּאֱמֶֽת׃
records.gloss: And it will be in day the that, not will add again [the] remnant of Israel and [the] escaped of [the] house of Jacob to lean on [the one] striking it, and it will lean on Yahweh, [the] Holy One of Israel, in truth.
pieces: On that day the remnant of Israel, those of the house of Jacob who have escaped, \q will no longer lean on the one who struck them down. \q Their support will be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the Holy One of Israel, in all faithfulness.

L.20: And it will be in that day, the remnant of Israel and the escaped of the house of Jacob \q will no longer again lean on the one who struck them, \q but will lean on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.

R.20: At that time the people left alive in Israel, the ones from Jacob's family who escape, \q will no longer depend on the nation that beat them down. \q Instead they will truly trust {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the Holy One of Israel.

decisions.choice: remnant, escaped: those left after the judgment
decisions.reason: The remnant is what is left over; the escaped are those who got away alive. Both name the small part of Israel that survives the Assyrian judgment and comes back to God (1:9; 4:2-3).

decisions.choice: lean on the one who struck them: trust in Assyria
decisions.reason: King Ahaz leaned on Assyria for help against Aram and Israel (7:1-17; 2 Kings 16:7-9), and Assyria became the power that struck Judah. The remnant will stop trusting in such help.

decisions.choice: in truth: faithfully, sincerely
decisions.reason: The word means firmness, faithfulness and truth. Their trust will be real and lasting, not in words only.

decisions.choice: the people left alive in Israel ... Jacob's family
decisions.reason: Readable explains "remnant" and "house of Jacob".

records.heading: A remnant will return

records.source: שְׁאָ֥ר יָשׁ֖וּב שְׁאָ֣ר יַעֲקֹ֑ב אֶל־אֵ֖ל גִּבּֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: A remnant will return, [the] remnant of Jacob, to God mighty.
pieces: A remnant will return, Jacob's remnant, \q to the Mighty God.

L.21: A remnant will return, [the] remnant of Jacob, \q to [the] mighty God.

R.21: Only a few will be left, but those few from Jacob's family will come back to the Mighty God.

decisions.choice: a remnant will return: the name of Isaiah's son Shear-jashub
decisions.reason: The two words are the name of the son Isaiah took with him to meet Ahaz (7:3). The name carried both a warning (only a remnant) and a promise (a remnant will return).

decisions.choice: return: come back to God, and come home
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn back. With "to the Mighty God" it means to turn back to God in repentance and trust (verse 20; 1:27; 6:10). It may also include coming home from exile.

decisions.choice: the Mighty God: the title of 9:5 (Hebrew numbering)
decisions.reason: The same two words are among the names of the child born for the throne of David in 9:5. Here they name the God to whom the remnant returns.

records.source: כִּ֣י אִם־יִהְיֶ֞ה עַמְּךָ֤ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כְּח֣וֹל הַיָּ֔ם שְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב בּ֑וֹ כִּלָּי֥וֹן חָר֖וּץ שׁוֹטֵ֥ף צְדָקָֽה׃
records.gloss: For though will be your people, Israel, like [the] sand of the sea, a remnant will return in it; destruction [is] determined, overflowing [with] righteousness.
pieces: Even if your people, Israel, are as many as the grains of sand by the sea, \q only a remnant within them will return. \q An end has been decided, and it comes flooding in with justice.

L.22: For though your people, Israel, be like the sand of the sea, \q a remnant within it will return; \q destruction [is] decreed, overflowing [with] righteousness.

R.22: People of Israel, even if there are as many of you as there are grains of sand on the beach, \q only a few will come back. \q God has decided to destroy, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} judgment will sweep over the land like a flood. It will be completely fair.

decisions.choice: like the sand of the sea: the promise to Abraham
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham descendants like the sand on the seashore (Genesis 22:17; 32:13). Even if that promise is kept in full, only a remnant will survive the judgment and return.

decisions.choice: a remnant will return: quoted in Romans 9:27-28
decisions.reason: Paul quotes verses 22-23 from the Greek Septuagint in Romans 9:27-28, to show that God saves a remnant of Israel by his grace.

decisions.choice: destruction decreed, overflowing with righteousness: a just judgment that sweeps over like a flood
decisions.reason: "Determined" means settled, cut and fixed. "Overflowing" pictures a flood (8:7-8; 28:15). "Righteousness" here is God's justice, the right he does in judging.

decisions.choice: only a remnant
decisions.reason: "Only" is implied by the contrast with the sand of the sea.

decisions.choice: justice
decisions.reason: The word usually rendered righteousness here means God's just judgment, so Balanced says "justice"; Literal keeps "righteousness".

decisions.choice: God has decided ... It will be completely fair.
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who decides and explains "righteousness" as a fair judgment.

records.source: כִּ֥י כָלָ֖ה וְנֶחֱרָצָ֑ה אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת עֹשֶׂ֖ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃ס
records.gloss: For complete destruction and [what is] determined [the] Lord Yahweh of hosts [is] making in [the] midst of all the land.
pieces: For the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies \q is about to bring a full and settled end within the whole land.

L.23: For a full end, and [one] decreed, \q the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of hosts is making in the midst of all the land.

R.23: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies has made up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind to bring this destruction on the whole land.

decisions.choice: a full end, and one decreed: a phrase of final judgment
decisions.reason: The same pair of words appears in 28:22 and in Daniel 9:27. The end God has decided will certainly come.

decisions.choice: the land: the land of Israel, or the earth
decisions.reason: The word means land or earth. In context it most likely means the land of God's people; the Greek of Romans 9:28 has "on the earth".

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת אַל־תִּירָ֥א עַמִּ֛י יֹשֵׁ֥ב צִיּ֖וֹן מֵֽאַשּׁ֑וּר בַּשֵּׁ֣בֶט יַכֶּ֔כָּה וּמַטֵּ֥הוּ יִשָּֽׂא־עָלֶ֖יךָ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh of hosts: do not be afraid, my people [who] dwell [in] Zion, of Assyria; with the rod he strikes you, and his staff he lifts against you in [the] way of Egypt.
pieces: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: \q Do not fear Assyria, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people who live in Zion. \q He strikes you with the rod \q and raises his staff over you the way Egypt did.

L.24: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of hosts: \q Do not be afraid of Assyria, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people who dwell [in] Zion; \q with the rod he strikes you, \q and his staff he lifts up against you in the way of Egypt.

R.24: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: \q My people who live in Zion, do not be afraid of the Assyrians. \q They beat you with sticks and raise clubs against you, just as the Egyptians did long ago.

decisions.choice: in the way of Egypt: as Egypt oppressed Israel
decisions.reason: Assyria treats God's people as Egypt did when Israel was enslaved there (Exodus 1-5). In verse 26 the same phrase turns: God will lift his staff as he did in Egypt, when he set his people free.

decisions.choice: do not be afraid, my people: comfort after judgment
decisions.reason: The judgment of verses 5-23 is real, but God still calls Zion "my people". Assyria's blows will soon end (verse 25).

decisions.choice: the Assyrians ... the Egyptians did long ago
decisions.reason: Readable names the peoples and explains that Egypt's oppression was long past.

records.source: כִּי־ע֖וֹד מְעַ֣ט מִזְעָ֑ר וְכָ֣לָה זַ֔עַם וְאַפִּ֖י עַל־תַּבְלִיתָֽם׃
records.gloss: For yet a little, a little, and will be finished [the] indignation, and my anger [will be] on their destruction.
pieces: For only a little while longer, \q and the fury will be spent; \q then {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger will turn to their ruin.

L.25: For yet a very little [while], \q and [the] indignation will be finished, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger [will turn] to their destruction.

R.25: Very soon I will stop being angry with you. \q Then {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger will turn against the Assyrians, and I will destroy them.

decisions.choice: a little, a little: a very short time
decisions.reason: The repeated word stresses how short the time will be (16:14; 29:17).

decisions.choice: the indignation ... their destruction: God's anger moves from his people to Assyria
decisions.reason: The indignation against God's people will come to an end (verse 5 used the same word). "Their" is the Assyrians: God's anger will be turned to destroying them.

decisions.choice: with you ... against the Assyrians
decisions.reason: Readable says whom the anger was against and whom it will now be against.

records.source: וְעוֹרֵ֨ר עָלָ֜יו יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ שׁ֔וֹט כְּמַכַּ֥ת מִדְיָ֖ן בְּצ֣וּר עוֹרֵ֑ב וּמַטֵּ֨הוּ֙ עַל־הַיָּ֔ם וּנְשָׂא֖וֹ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And will wield against him Yahweh of hosts a whip, like [the] striking of Midian at [the] rock of Oreb; and his staff [is] over the sea, and he will lift it in [the] way of Egypt.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies will crack a whip over him, \q as in the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb. \q His staff will be over the sea, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will lift it up as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did in Egypt.

L.26: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts will wield a whip against him, \q like the striking of Midian at the rock of Oreb; \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} staff [will be] over the sea, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will lift it up in the way of Egypt.

R.26: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies will attack the Assyrians with a whip. \q It will be like the time Gideon defeated the Midianites at the rock of Oreb. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will hold {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} staff out over the sea, \q the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did in Egypt long ago.

decisions.choice: the striking of Midian at the rock of Oreb: Gideon's victory
decisions.reason: In Judges 7:25 the Midianite leader Oreb was killed at a rock that took his name, when God gave Gideon victory over a great army with a few men. Isaiah recalled the same day of Midian in 9:3 (Hebrew numbering).

decisions.choice: his staff over the sea ... in the way of Egypt: the crossing of the Red Sea
decisions.reason: At the sea Moses lifted his staff over the water at God's command, and Egypt's army was drowned (Exodus 14:16, 26-27). "In the way of Egypt" in verse 24 meant the way Egypt oppressed; here it means the way God rescued his people from Egypt.

decisions.choice: as he did in Egypt
decisions.reason: "In the way of Egypt" here refers to what God did there, so Balanced supplies "as he did".

decisions.choice: the Assyrians ... Gideon
decisions.reason: Readable names "him" as the Assyrians and names Gideon, the leader in Judges 7.

records.source: וְהָיָ֣ה׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יָס֤וּר סֻבֳּלוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל שִׁכְמֶ֔ךָ וְעֻלּ֖וֹ מֵעַ֣ל צַוָּארֶ֑ךָ וְחֻבַּ֥ל עֹ֖ל מִפְּנֵי־שָֽׁמֶן׃
records.gloss: And it will be in day the that, will be removed his burden from on your shoulder, and his yoke from on your neck, and will be broken [the] yoke because of fatness.
pieces: On that day the load he laid on your shoulder will be taken away, \q and his yoke off your neck. \q The yoke will snap because of fatness.

L.27: And it will be in that day, his burden will be removed from your shoulder \q and his yoke from your neck, \q and [the] yoke will be broken because of fatness.

R.27: At that time, Assyria's heavy load will be taken off your shoulders. \q The yoke Assyria put on your neck will be taken away. \q The yoke will break, like a yoke that breaks when the ox grows too big and strong for it.

decisions.choice: his burden ... his yoke: Assyria's rule lifted
decisions.reason: "His" is Assyria. The same picture of a broken yoke and a lifted burden is in 9:3 (Hebrew numbering) and 14:25.

decisions.choice: because of fatness: the yoke breaks because the neck has grown strong
alternatives: the start of the march in verse 28
decisions.reason: The words are hard. They most likely mean that the ox has grown so fat and strong that its yoke breaks. The word can also mean oil, and some read it as "because of the anointing". Others take the last word with the march of verse 28, as a place from which the enemy comes up.

decisions.choice: like a yoke that breaks when the ox grows too big and strong for it
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the most likely sense of "fatness".

records.source: בָּ֥א עַל־עַיַּ֖ת עָבַ֣ר בְּמִגְר֑וֹן לְמִכְמָ֖שׂ יַפְקִ֥יד כֵּלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: He has come to Aiath; he has passed through Migron; at Michmash he deposits his baggage.
pieces: He has reached Aiath and marched through Migron; \q at Michmash he leaves his baggage.

L.28: He has come to Aiath; he has passed through Migron; \q at Michmash he deposits his baggage.

R.28: The enemy army has reached the town of Aiath. It has gone through Migron. \q At Michmash the soldiers leave their heavy supplies.

decisions.choice: Aiath, Migron, Michmash: towns north of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Verses 28-32 picture an enemy marching south toward Jerusalem from town to town, each closer than the last. Aiath is Ai (Joshua 7-8; Nehemiah 11:31); Michmash is where Jonathan fought the Philistines (1 Samuel 13-14). The march ends within sight of the city (verse 32).

decisions.choice: he has come: the enemy is not named
decisions.reason: The verbs are vivid, as though the prophet sees the march happening. The one marching is not named, but in context it is the Assyrian king of verses 5-15.

decisions.choice: deposits his baggage: leaves the heavy supplies behind
decisions.reason: An army left its heavy gear in a camp before moving fast against a city (1 Samuel 17:22).

decisions.choice: The enemy army
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject the Hebrew leaves unnamed, without saying which army it is.

records.source: עָֽבְרוּ֙ מַעְבָּרָ֔ה גֶּ֖בַע מָל֣וֹן לָ֑נוּ חָֽרְדָה֙ הָֽרָמָ֔ה גִּבְעַ֥ת שָׁא֖וּל נָֽסָה׃
records.gloss: They have crossed the pass; Geba [is] a lodging for us; Ramah has trembled; Gibeah of Saul has fled.
pieces: They have gone across the pass: \q "Geba will be our camp for the night!" \q Ramah is trembling; \q Gibeah of Saul has taken flight.

L.29: They have crossed the pass: \q "Geba [is] a lodging for us!" \q Ramah trembles; \q Gibeah of Saul has fled.

R.29: The soldiers have crossed the narrow pass. \q They say, "We will camp tonight at Geba!" \q The people of Ramah are shaking with fear. \q The people of Gibeah, King Saul's hometown, have run away.

decisions.choice: the pass, Geba: the gorge between Michmash and Geba
decisions.reason: A deep, narrow valley separates Michmash from Geba (1 Samuel 13:23; 14:4-5). Crossing it brought the army into Judah's own land.

decisions.choice: Geba is a lodging for us: the soldiers' words
decisions.reason: The words are spoken by the army: they will spend the night at Geba. They may also be read as a statement, "they lodged at Geba".

decisions.choice: Ramah, Gibeah of Saul
decisions.reason: Ramah was Samuel's town (1 Samuel 7:17); Gibeah was Saul's home and royal seat (1 Samuel 10:26). Both were a few miles north of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: The people of Ramah ... King Saul's hometown
decisions.reason: Readable says that the towns stand for their people and explains Gibeah of Saul.

records.source: צַהֲלִ֥י קוֹלֵ֖ךְ בַּת־גַּלִּ֑ים הַקְשִׁ֥יבִי לַ֖יְשָׁה עֲנִיָּ֥ה עֲנָתֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Cry aloud [with] your voice, daughter of Gallim! Pay attention, Laishah! Afflicted [one], Anathoth!
pieces: Raise your voice and cry, Daughter Gallim! \q Take heed, Laishah! Afflicted Anathoth!

L.30: Cry shrill [with] your voice, daughter of Gallim! \q Pay attention, Laishah! Afflicted [one], Anathoth!

R.30: People of Gallim, scream for help! \q People of Laishah, listen! Poor people of Anathoth!

decisions.choice: daughter of Gallim: the town of Gallim and its people
decisions.reason: As in "daughter Zion", "daughter" names a town as a woman, and so its people (1:8).

decisions.choice: afflicted, Anathoth: poor Anathoth
decisions.reason: The word means afflicted or wretched and sounds like the town's name, Anathoth, the home of the priest Abiathar and of Jeremiah (1 Kings 2:26; Jeremiah 1:1). With a change of vowels it can be read "answer her, Anathoth", one town echoing another's cry.

decisions.choice: People of Gallim ... People of Laishah ... Poor people of Anathoth
decisions.reason: Readable names the people of each town.

records.source: נָדְדָ֖ה מַדְמֵנָ֑ה יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הַגֵּבִ֖ים הֵעִֽיזוּ׃
records.gloss: Has fled Madmenah; [the] inhabitants of Gebim have brought to safety.
pieces: Madmenah has run away; \q those who live in Gebim have hurried their goods to safety.

L.31: Madmenah has fled; \q the inhabitants of Gebim have brought [their goods] to safety.

R.31: The people of Madmenah have run away. \q The people of Gebim have taken their things and hurried to a safe place.

decisions.choice: have brought to safety: carried off their goods, taken refuge
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring something into a safe place (Exodus 9:19; Jeremiah 4:6). The people of Gebim gather what they can and flee.

decisions.choice: Madmenah, Gebim: small towns near Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Their exact places are not known; they lay on the way to Jerusalem from the north.

records.source: ע֥וֹד הַיּ֖וֹם בְּנֹ֣ב לַֽעֲמֹ֑ד יְנֹפֵ֤ף יָדוֹ֙ הַ֣ר בַּת־צִיּ֔וֹן גִּבְעַ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: Yet the day at Nob to stand; he will shake his hand [at the] mountain of [the] daughter of Zion, [the] hill of Jerusalem.
pieces: Before this day is over he will stand at Nob, \q waving his fist toward the mountain of Daughter Zion, \q toward Jerusalem's hill.

L.32: Yet this day [he is] at Nob to stand; \q he will shake his hand [at the] mountain of the daughter of Zion, \q the hill of Jerusalem.

R.32: This very day the enemy will stop at the town of Nob. \q From there he will shake his fist at Mount Zion, \q the hill where Jerusalem stands.

decisions.choice: Nob: the last stop, close to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Nob was a town of priests (1 Samuel 21-22) close to Jerusalem on the north (Nehemiah 11:32). From there the enemy can see the city.

decisions.choice: shake his hand: threaten
decisions.reason: Shaking one's hand at a city is a gesture of threat and scorn. The march stops here: the next verse tells what God does.

decisions.choice: daughter of Zion: the reading of the margin
decisions.reason: The written text has "house of Zion"; the reading in the margin has "daughter of Zion", the phrase Isaiah uses elsewhere (1:8; 16:1, where the same line returns).

decisions.choice: Mount Zion
decisions.reason: Readable says "Mount Zion" for "the mountain of the daughter of Zion".

records.source: הִנֵּ֤ה הָאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת מְסָעֵ֥ף פֻּארָ֖ה בְּמַעֲרָצָ֑ה וְרָמֵ֤י הַקּוֹמָה֙ גְּדוּעִ֔ים וְהַגְּבֹהִ֖ים יִשְׁפָּֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: Look, the Lord, Yahweh of hosts, [is] lopping off boughs with a terrifying crash, and the exalted ones of height [are] cut down, and the high ones will be brought low.
pieces: Look! The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies is about to strip away the boughs with a terrifying crash. \q The trees that tower highest will be cut down; \q the proud heights will be laid low.

L.33: Look, the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of hosts [is] lopping off boughs with a terrifying crash; \q and the high [ones] of stature [are] cut down, \q and the lofty will be brought low.

R.33: But look! The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies is ready to chop off the branches with a terrible crash. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will cut down the tallest trees, those proud and powerful enemies, and bring them down low.

decisions.choice: look, the Lord: God acts at the last moment
decisions.reason: At the very point where the enemy shakes his fist at Jerusalem (verse 32), God acts. In 701 BC the Assyrian army of Sennacherib withdrew from Jerusalem without taking it (37:36-37).

decisions.choice: the high ones brought low: God humbles the proud
decisions.reason: The words echo 2:12-17, where all that is high and lifted up, the cedars of Lebanon among them, is brought low on the LORD's day. Here the tall trees are the Assyrian king and his army (verses 12, 18).

decisions.choice: a terrifying crash: terror, a dreadful sound
decisions.reason: The rare word means a frightening thing; with the lopping of branches it pictures the crash of falling boughs.

decisions.choice: those proud and powerful enemies
decisions.reason: Readable says that the trees stand for the enemy.

records.source: וְנִקַּ֛ף סִֽבְכֵ֥י הַיַּ֖עַר בַּבַּרְזֶ֑ל וְהַלְּבָנ֖וֹן בְּאַדִּ֥יר יִפּֽוֹל׃ס
records.gloss: And he will cut down [the] thickets of the forest with the iron, and the Lebanon by a mighty one will fall.
pieces: He will hack down the tangled forest with iron, \q and Lebanon will come crashing down by a mighty one.

L.34: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, \q and Lebanon will fall by a mighty one.

R.34: He will cut down the thick forest with an iron ax. \q Even Lebanon, with its great trees, will fall to someone mighty.

decisions.choice: the forest, Lebanon: the might of Assyria
decisions.reason: Lebanon was famous for its great cedars (2:13; 37:24). Here the forest stands for Assyria's army and power, felled like trees. In 11:1 a new shoot will grow from the stump of Jesse: the forest of Assyria is cut down for good, but the house of David will sprout again.

decisions.choice: a mighty one: God, or a mighty ax
decisions.reason: The word means majestic or mighty. It most likely points to God himself, the Majestic One (33:21). It may also describe the iron tool that fells the trees.

decisions.choice: he will cut down: the Lord of verse 33
alternatives: the thickets of the forest will be cut down
decisions.reason: The subject is the Lord who lops the boughs in verse 33. The verb can also be read as passive, "the thickets will be cut down".
